steps.content: Three hours ago

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: I like it here. Suits me better than anywhere else.
The hem of her dress trailing behind, Irrheia settles into the interrogation chair without needing any prompting from the staff. She finds a comfortable position and seems completely at ease.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You like it here? Good. We're about to begin your interrogation. It's always better when we're on the same page.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: It's not that I like this place. I just detest boredom. If you can provide me with a nice little surprise, I can be quite cooperative. My dear Chief, how this "interrogation" unfolds is entirely up to you. Don't disappoint me, okay?
She's adept at dominating a conversation, but you've dealt with your fair share of highly confident, hard-to-read Sinners. You know not to appear intimidated.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So it's thrills you're after? Then I imagine you must be quite pleased with the Bureau. After all, you often invite other Sinners to participate in your "Life Swap" murder mystery game. You've even made a few friends, haven't you?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Oh... you mean their experiences and personal stories? Their life choices were indeed quite extreme and fascinating, even Mania itself is drawn to them... You could say I came here specifically to experience them.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Unfortunately, even the legendary MBCC, where madness and taboos gather, doesn't seem to offer enough novelty. I grew tired of it all rather quickly. Fortunately, Mess and Etti came to my aid, devising new games better suited to my abilities.
The nib of your pen stops.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You mean... the "swap"?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Yes, swapping our scripts and our lives. I was curious to see how they would behave in my scripts and what endings they might reach. Sinners who scorn rules would certainly discover more fascinating possibilities, better ways to solve problems, more audacious choices...

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: And they delivered, they truly did. Unfortunately, there are only so many interesting individuals, even here. My dear Chief, if you're hoping these games alone will keep me here, then you've gravely underestimated the long-time feud I've had with boredom. I need more.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Can you offer what I require?

Your palms grow clammy with sweat. You realize your decision to immediately press the interrogation once that opening appeared was correct. You know adrenaline-addicted Sinners like Irrheia are notoriously difficult to manage, and sure enough, your time was almost up.

Observing the Sinner's relaxed demeanor, you recognize her confessions are likely just another tactic to extract more surprises and entertainment from you. The fact that she's still here means you still have a chance.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why can't I? What you crave is excitement, not malice or madness. Those aren't the same thing. Or perhaps... you're deliberately trying to mislead me? Too bad for you, I've seen far too much to be fooled. I know people like you never speak plainly.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Oh, really? Please share your unique and fascinating theory, in that case.
Your unwavering confidence may not have pleased her, but it has at least held her attention. Irrheia doesn't look offended. Instead, she smiles and gestures with her hand for you to continue.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You want me to believe you use these scripts to manipulate participants purely for your own amusement, that you deliberately push them toward madness, permanently altering their real-life personalities. But that narrative doesn't hold up.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Most of your clients, including Sinners, were actually positively affected by their experiences. True, some did become more aggressive, but our investigation proved they had already committed crimes before. They were simply better at hiding their true nature.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When someone's actions contradict their words, I always trust the actions. Irrheia, your actions reveal you're not completely amoral. You still have a fundamental sense of right and wrong, and chaos is not your only desire.

As you speak, you watch Irrheia's seemingly perfect, ethereal smile without blinking, hoping your words might probe a crack in her carefully constructed facade. But her smile remains fixed, as if carved in stone.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: A captivating analysis. True, I would never claim to seek madness or malice for their own sake. I simply accept anything that breaks the mundane existence. But make no mistake. Morality has never influenced my decisions, and it never will.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: I simply want those I invite into my scenarios to bring me the greatest thrills and twists. It's mere coincidence that actions driven by this principle happened to produce results matching your observations. Nothing more.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Perhaps you're right. Coincidences do exist. For example... your parents and brother. They just happened to be the source of your tedious existence, so you decided to guide them through your scenarios to spice up your life. Isn't that right?

She evaded your analysis effortlessly. Rather than pressing your point, you pretend to take a step back, following her logic. Then, just as she begins to lose interest, you launch your counterattack, revealing the crucial information that brought you here in the first place.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: ...You've done your research thoroughly, my dear Chief.

Your strategy works. Irrheia doesn't immediately drop her smile, but you clearly notice the way her breath catches and her fingertips tap the armrest upon hearing the new information, as if trying to mask her momentary surprise. You press your advantage.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Irrheia Ashworth. Your parents are Tullian and Serena, and your brother is Raymond. Your family is old money in the pharmaceutical technology industry. Family history of a hereditary disease. The incidence rate is low, but once diagnosed, one would require long-term blood donations from close relatives in large quantities.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There are no explicit diagnosis records for Raymond, but he resided in a sanatorium for years. You were born shortly after his relocation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's quite a coincidence already. But even more coincidentally, you left your family and appeared in Eastside right after the Ashworths announced their technical breakthrough and the discovery of a cure for that hereditary disease.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: According to a board secretary, around the same time, the Ashworth family suddenly underwent a complete transformation. Once "cold, selfish, and pretentious," they began taking an interest in charitable causes and sometimes displayed stress responses that made them look "mentally unstable."

You flip through the file, rustling the pages. The warm sheets are freshly printed, yet the sound of them cutting through the air feels strangely familiar, like the oppressive past cycles that loom over everyone. You know that neither you nor Irrheia are strangers to this sound.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Does this description sound familiar? I imagine many of your regular guests exhibited similar symptoms, just not as severe. That makes sense, given these were likely the very first "customers" you used your ability on.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Let me guess. You were created and exploited by your family for a single purpose, so you chose vengeance once you acquired your ability. The family that treated you as a medical resource became the first prey to your special power, isn't that right?

Organize the information, theorize, then question. This is your well-practiced routine in the interrogation room. You scrutinize every subtle shift in Irrheia's expression, only to find, with disappointment, that the momentary vulnerability has vanished as you dig deeper.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: To be honest, I expected more from you. The facts themselves can't be changed, but there are countless ways to connect them, yet you chose the most predictable one.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: I won't deny that my birth was "intentional," and my life was carefully planned out, but my family possessed enough wealth that they didn't need to deprive me of anything. Likewise, my parents and my brother never laid a finger on me, nor did they break a single law.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Their only "crime"... was perhaps simply being too boring. When I gained my ability and realized I could experience more than my daily schedule, when I pictured those thrills and surprises... inevitably, I had to leave my family behind.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: But I didn't know this at the time. After gaining my ability, I returned home, still expecting their guidance, only to discover they were unbearably conventional and astonishingly dull. That's when I realized what I truly needed was to be free of any inhibition.
Her expression remains casual as she speaks, but you detect an almost sardonic entitlement and contempt in her voice.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: After that, I stopped caring about them. Their fault for being so bland. What you're describing might be some kind of "side effect," but what does it matter? I've lost interest in their stories. You shouldn't bother either.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: My family was merely a rather dull prologue to my life, a setup before I discovered my true calling. That's a significant enough role for such plain side characters, wouldn't you agree?
The arrogance and indifference in Irrheia's tone seem genuine, and you don't believe an S-Class Sinner would hesitate to own up to her revenge, yet you remain skeptical.

If there truly is no "hidden trauma" in her past, then what shaped Irrheia into who she is today? Her background is too well-documented, too easily verified. You're convinced something crucial lies in the gaps between these facts.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Let me guess, you're not convinced by what I've said? I don't mind your persistence, and I understand that truth lies in facts. But just what kind of "truth" are you hoping to extract from me?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Don't say I didn't warn you. What people tell you is never the truth, just stories.

You observe her composed, unhurried demeanor. She seems utterly confident that you have no choice but to accept her answers. You, too, are well aware that interrogation, or mere conversation, has its limitations.
But you never accept your defeat without fighting back.

options: But your script can tell the truth.

choices.text: But your script can tell the truth.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You mentioned that you've let many Sinners experience the script of your life, curious to see what endings they would create in your place. So this script must tell a story that's very close to the truth.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I want to see this version of the truth. Let me into your script.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Oh? I see, that's been your goal from the very start. Interesting. But what makes you think I still keep it?
Your unexpected request seems to have finally sparked genuine interest in Irrheia. She studies you with curiosity, her smile, usually as fixed as a printed illustration, finally widens.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: As I said before, few could reach thrilling endings. The buildup was tediously long and dull, and the payoff wasn't worth the wait... And I certainly don't keep things that bore me so much.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That has indeed been my goal from the beginning. After all, you carelessly discarded it without noticing that it still contained detectable traces of Mania.

You pull out a tattered page from the file and place it at the edge of the desk. Irrheia's expression freezes momentarily in surprise, but it quickly melts into a wider, wilder smile brimming with anticipation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is certainly not enough to create a fully immersive experience for ordinary people or even Sinners, but I'm different. My shackles will allow me to delve deeper into Mania. These remaining fragments are still useful to me.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Perhaps so. But I've intentionally severed my control over this script. I might still be able to bring you into it, but I can't guarantee I'll have any control once we're there. In other words, this script is unpredictable and dangerous for you.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: This time, I can't rewrite the story in real time to ensure a controlled experience, so you may not be able to reach a good ending. And if that was the case... you might actually die.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If even the most uninhibited Sinners can no longer surprise you, then aren't I your only hope left?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm capable of controlling Sinners. Aren't you curious to see the outcome when you put the uncontrollable me in this uncontrollable script? As for the danger... isn't that the best part for you?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Think of it as a gamble, or a deal I'm offering you. I'm betting I can reach what you call a good ending while obtaining what I need and come out alive. Meanwhile, you'll get to witness exactly what you're hoping to see.
Irrheia smiles and reaches for the thin sheet, its corner slicing through the air. You hear a loud flipping sound.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Very well. I never turn down anything that might relieve my boredom... even if only for a fleeting moment.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Don't disappoint me, my dear Chief.

You time your actions to match both Irrheia's movements and the flowing Mania in the interrogation room. Then, you release your shackles. Red spikes spiral upward, this time not to restrain, but to connect.

After absorbing the flood of memories, everything falls silent. Even Irrheia's presence fades away, vanishing alongside the rustling of turning pages. The mirror still shows her childhood face, but you clearly recognize yourself behind those eyes.
You remember what you're looking for and your purpose for coming here. This white hospital room, this life governed by endless measurements and precise schedules... they make up Irrheia's past.
"They never laid a finger on me, nor did they break a single law. Their only crime was simply being too boring." ...To think she was actually telling the truth.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But that doesn't mean she really did reveal everything. Without experiencing it firsthand, no one could truly understand how mind-numbingly boring a "properly regulated" life could be.

You look around the room. No books. No television. Only a single notebook rests on the nightstand. Every form of stimulation and entertainment has been removed, leaving you alone with nothing but your own thoughts for company.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...I'm beginning to understand her now. Trapped in here indefinitely, surrounded by the same white walls, the same unchanging routine, anyone would desperately want to escape... to feel something, anything.

In this stark environment, every breath and heartbeat seems unnaturally amplified, so clearly audible that it becomes disturbing. Time seems to stretch and crawl. You lose track of how long you've been lost in thought, or how much longer you must endure this empty contemplation.
A life wrapped in cotton wool may be safe and healthy, but it's also sterile and bland. You don't even feel alive. It's the exact opposite of what you experienced in Cirrenfold.

There's no compelling storyline here, no fantastical imagination, no plot twists to shake things up. Only the slow, predictable rhythm of unchanging routine. This is the tedious existence Irrheia fought against and ultimately fled.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But understanding doesn't help. At least, understanding alone can't solve the fundamental problem: How to escape from here.
Irrheia has long broken free from this past on her own. This is now your prison. Only by reaching the so-called "good ending" can you return to reality with this newfound insight about her.

You look up and meet the eyes of "Irrheia" in the mirror. You mutter to yourself, partly to organize your thoughts through the persistent headache, and partly because you know she's watching you with keen interest from somewhere. Your struggles and attempts are precisely the variables she so desperately craves.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She hates anything mundane, predictable, or uncreative. She loves excitement, change, and novelty. So the strategy should be to follow the residual instincts in this body, guess her "previous" choices, then stay as far away from them as possible... That approach should work.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But after seven resets, I'm still trapped here. That means something's not working. Maybe I'm not deviating enough from her choices? Just how different must the choices be to break this cycle?

You need to keep trying, but as Irrheia warned, each failure erodes your consciousness further. Your time is running out. You struggle to concentrate, but the mental fog grows thicker by the moment, like dragging your thoughts through cold mud.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: More fascinating possibilities, better ways to solve problems, more audacious choices...
The "good ending" in her mind comes down to these three elements. And they represent not only my way out, but also my realization of what she truly desires...
This should be the only goal and the only approach.

You gaze around the desolate, lifeless hospital room where endless white threatens to smother every thought. You understand that within this place you return to after each reset, hidden in this suffocating whiteness, lies a gap into Irrheia's soul.
And only by reaching her most profound desire can you hope to break this endless cycle.

options: And you'll break the cycle thoroughly

choices.text: And you'll break the cycle thoroughly

steps.content: You stand up decisively, push the door open, and walk out. The inertia of the script makes each step a struggle, but it's exactly this exhausting trudging sensation that confirms you're moving toward something entirely different from the predetermined story. The right path.

steps.speaker: Young Man
steps.content: ...Irria? What are you doing here? Who brought you?

You thank the nurse who mistakenly thinks you're just being a caring sister, and enter the obviously cozier suite. You don't expect a welcome, but your wretched brother's unkindness still manages to surprise you.

Not only does he get your name wrong, but he also makes no effort to hide his irritation. Only after his gaze passes over the IV drip steadily feeding into his arm does he seem to remember his role as a brother.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: My name is Irrheia. No one brought me. I came on my own.

steps.speaker: Young Man
steps.content: On your own? You? Irrheia, I don't know what you've heard from the person who brought you here, but it's all lies. Neither the family nor I have ever wronged you. If you're smart enough, you should...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm not smart, nor do I wish to be. Pragmatism only works when circumstances already favor you.
Ignoring his condescending lecture, you slowly approach him, then suddenly leap onto the bed, using every ounce of strength to pin him down by his chest and clamp your hand firmly over his mouth!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Take you, for instance. Always on the high ground, waiting for them to feed you the sacrificial blood. You even have the audacity to complain about the taste. But circumstances will never be in the sacrifice's favor, no matter how long I wait.

He's the older brother, and you're in the body of his younger sister. But ironically, the disease that exploits you has left him weak, while the strict regimen designed to facilitate that exploitation has made you strong. You've pinned him down with surprising ease.

steps.speaker: Young Man
steps.content: What... are you... doing...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I want to break this scripted, controlled, meaningless routine! I want to break free from the indoctrinated ideals of sacrifice and duty! I want to shatter this damned cycle where I'm used as a mere disposable blood bag!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A life that can only be sustained by sucking another's blood should not exist! No one is born to be exploited and consumed! All this talk of sacrifice and duty is complete nonsense! You can't take my life away with these manipulative tactics anymore!

You stare into his panicked, terrified eyes, knowing full well this isn't the actual person who oppressed Irrheia for years, but a mere phantom. Yet your words aren't false. They flow from your lips naturally, like an instinctive, reflexive response.

You no longer have to fight against this body. Every movement has become effortless and fluid, as if someone else is guiding your hands to make the same motions, adding their strength to yours, just as Irrheia once did.

Is this what Irrheia truly wanted all along? Had she wished to see through the deception sooner? To make her escape sooner? Or even shatter these constraints and confront these people who twisted her life with tedium and control earlier?

steps.speaker: Young Man
steps.content: Who... who are you really... You're not my sister...!

steps.speaker: Young Man
steps.content: No one has taught her these things. How could she possibly know any of this...?!

He struggles with every ounce of his strength, suddenly unleashing a surprising burst of power that sends you flying off him. You crash hard onto the floor and see him scramble to the edge of the bed and slam his fist on the security alarm!
BEEEEEEEP!

The piercing alarm cuts through the air and seems to slice right into your skull. Your vision explodes with dark spots, and you barely make out the uniformed personnel rushing into the room. But before they can even grab you, the entire scene begins to crumble.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...A reset?!

A wave of excruciating pain washes over you, followed by a loud thud. Your mind finally shuts down like a power outage, plunging into a complete blank. Before you can even feel the relief, one final thought flashes past your mind.
Where did it go wrong this time?
